info.title: PandaOPDS
info.description: PandaOPDS management and reading API. Basic authentication applies when both AUTH_USERNAME and AUTH_PASSWORD are configured, subject to configured path exemptions. E-Hentai account credentials are configured server-side. Archive start and refresh can spend GP.

get.description:
Root OPDS 1.2 navigation feed (hard-coded, no home.toml).

Pure standard navigation: Latest / Watched / Favorites / Popular /
Toplist (single entry; period facets live inside the toplist feed) +
a trailing protocol-level Search link.  Watched/Favorites are omitted
when no IPB cookie is configured.

get.description:

pagination uses `page` (1-based, `?p=` upstream) — not the lastGid
`next` mechanism used by the front-page feeds. Pure standard Atom, no
extensions (v1.2 constraint).

get.description:
Detail feed: archived galleries prefer cached online detail HTML and
fall back to the local archive snapshot when upstream is unavailable.

Fetching the detail page also pre-warms the page-URL mapping cache so the
first /stream request skips one upstream round trip.

get.description:
Root OPDS 2.0 document.

Layout is driven by a TOML config: ``[[group]]`` declares named groups;
``[[section]]`` references a group via ``group`` field.  Publication and
navigation sections can co-exist in the same group.

Sections without a ``group``:
* ``kind="publication"`` → standalone ``groups[]`` entry
* ``kind="navigation"``  → root ``navigation[]`` entry

Watched / Favorites are auth-gated: omitted when no IPB cookie is set.
The Archives preset (``query="archives"``) is store-gated: omitted
while the archive store holds no ready entries.

200.description: Navigation and available publication previews. The Go service waits up to 12 seconds for previews and marks the response no-store if the deadline is reached.

get.description:
Single-publication document: a top-level RWPM/OPDS publication object.

This is the target of every publication's `rel="self"` link. Clients
like Stump follow `self` to open details and read through the embedded
`readingOrder` (per-page image URLs); the response shape matches what
their parser expects (a publication object, not an acquisition feed).
Ready archives prefer online detail-page HTML and use the local snapshot
when upstream is unavailable.

get.description:
Proxy a cover/preview URL (settings.image_proxy_hosts) same-origin.

Comment content (x:reviews) may embed eh/ex cover images on a different
origin; a web client fetching them cross-origin hits CORS. This endpoint
fetches the exact bytes through the throttled, authenticated client and
serves them from the PandaOPDS origin. The URL is treated as opaque (no
gid/token parsing).

Single:  ``POST /api/favorites`` with ``{action, gid, token, favcat, note}``

get.description:
Flat favcat id -> name map (shortcut-friendly: plain JSON object).

Same cached data as /api/favorites/categories but shaped as
``{"0": "Favorites", "1": "Common", ...}`` so a quick-action script can
look a folder's real name up by id (or list names in id order) without
unwrapping an array.

post.description: Run a single favorites scan. If automatic archiving is configured, a scan after the initial baseline may submit archives and spend GP.

Purge the on-disk image cache.

Disk entries live up to 7 days, so stale bytes (e.g. thumbnails cached
before a cover-proxy fix) need an explicit clear. Memory caches are left
untouched — they hold URLs/metadata and expire within minutes/hours.
Route is covered by Basic Auth when enabled (same as the rest of WebUI).

archive_update_interval_days.description: Archive version check interval in days. The default is 7, 0 disables periodic checks, and null resets the default. Stored in settings.toml.

archive_auto_update.description: Automatically download newer archive versions, which may spend GP. Defaults to false. Stored in settings.toml.

favorites_sync_archive.description: Automatically archive newly discovered favorites, which may spend GP. Defaults to false. The initial scan only creates a baseline. Stored in settings.toml; environment overrides lock this setting.

favorites_sync_categories.description: Limits auto-archive scope using comma-separated favorite folder IDs 0-9; -ID excludes a folder; empty means all folders. It does not filter the sync scan. Stored in settings.toml; environment overrides lock this setting.
